findings.candidate_quote: Compounds 5c and 5e demonstrated high selectivity for BuChE over AChE, with over 150-fold selectivity, and showed protective effects against H2O2- and Aβ-induced toxicity by reducing ROS and upregulating antioxidant genes.
findings.reference_quote: Notably, although 5e exhibited superior BuChE selectivity (SI = 294.14) and potent enzyme inhibition, its relatively weak neuroprotective activity, particularly in the H2O2-induced oxidative stress model (53.57% viability), limited its potential as a multifunctional agent.
findings.explanation: This incorrectly includes 5e among the protective antioxidant leads. Its H2O2-treated viability was 53.57%, below the model’s 64.02%; the compounds selected for ROS and antioxidant-pathway experiments were 5c, 5g and 5h.

findings.candidate_quote: The findings reflect observed associations rather than definitive causal or clinical claims.
findings.reference_quote: All the tested compounds can significantly delay the Aβ42-induced paralysis at 10 μM.
findings.explanation: The blanket association characterization understates experimental evidence from compound administration in cells and nematodes. These interventions support causal treatment effects within the tested models, although they do not establish human efficacy or definitive pathway mediation.

findings.candidate_quote: Age-related debility was the most common cause of death in long-term survivors, followed by COVID-19 (5.0%) and cardiovascular collapse (1.4%).
findings.reference_quote: The leading causes of death among patients with IS who died from other causes were age-related debility (87.6%), COVID-19 (5.0%), and cardiovascular collapse (1.4%).
findings.explanation: The ranking and percentages apply within the “other causes” category across all periods, not to all long-term deaths. The summary incorrectly makes COVID-19 and cardiovascular collapse the next leading causes among long-term survivors.

findings.candidate_quote: A sensitivity analysis excluding pandemic-related deaths showed consistent mortality patterns.
findings.reference_quote: A sensitivity analysis excluding 115,709 patients (13.0%) who died during the pandemic period (2020–2022) was performed to examine mortality patterns in the absence of COVID-19 as a contributing cause of death.
findings.explanation: The analysis excluded all patients who died during 2020–2022, irrespective of cause. Describing these as pandemic-related deaths changes the exclusion criterion to deaths attributed to the pandemic.
